chunks: Some people from among his companions were present, including Abu Bakr and Umar. So he said, “O Abu Bakr, judge between them.” He said, “O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, one beast killed another beast; nothing is due upon it.” He said, “O Umar, judge between them.” He replied with the like of Abu Bakr’s statement. Then he said, “O Ali عليه السلام, judge between them.” He said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم: if the bull entered upon the donkey in its resting place, then the owners of the bull are liable; but if the donkey entered upon the bull in its resting place, then there is no liability upon them.”

He said: “Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم raised his hand toward the sky and said: Praise belongs to Allah, who has made from me one who judges with the judgment of the Prophets عليهم السلام.”
(902) 35 — From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Sabbah al-Hadhdha’, from a man, from Sa‘d ibn Tarif al-Iskaf, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام:
The like of that in meaning, though some of its wordings differed.

key_terms.الثَّوْرُ: The bull, one of the two animals in the ruling
key_terms.الْحِمَارُ: The donkey, the other animal in the ruling
key_terms.بَهِيمَةٌ: A domesticated animal or beast involved in the case
key_terms.بِقَضَاءِ النَّبِيِّينَ: In accordance with the judgment of the Prophets عليهم السلام
key_terms.ضَمَانَ: Legal liability or responsibility for damages
key_terms.مُسْتَرَاحِهِ: Its resting place or enclosure, which determines liability

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one animal kills another, and how did Imam Ali عليه السلام judge the case?
ai.summary: This report concerns liability when one animal kills another, establishing a legal distinction based on which animal entered the resting place of the other. It also highlights the superior judicial discernment of Imam Ali عليه السلام, whose ruling the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم praised as being in accordance with the judgments of the Prophets عليهم السلام.
